title: Designing Interactive Before-and-After Comparison Sliders and Medical Booking Flows in React
seoTitle: React Before/After Sliders & Medical Booking UI
description: Learn how to build a custom interactive before and after image comparison slider and multi-step medical appointment booking flow in React.

author.name: Aafaque Nazir
author.bio: Independent web engineer building high-performance websites, e-commerce stores, and SaaS web applications for clients across India & worldwide.

quickAnswer: A React before-and-after image slider tracks pointer coordinates over a container to clip the top image width dynamically, while a medical booking flow uses controlled multi-step state validation to submit patient appointments reliably.

faqs.question: How do you build a responsive before and after image slider in React?
faqs.answer: You track mouse move and touch move events on a parent container, calculate the cursor offset percentage from the left boundary, and apply that percentage as the width of the top clipped image layer.

faqs.question: What is the best way to handle multi-step medical booking forms in React?
faqs.answer: Use a local React state variable to track the active step index, validate user inputs at each step before allowing progression, and retain form data in a single parent state object until final submission.

faqs.question: Why are image comparison sliders important for dental and medical websites?
faqs.answer: They provide instant visual proof of clinical procedures such as teeth whitening, orthodontics, or cosmetic surgery, helping patients build trust and decide to book a consultation.

sections.title: Introduction to Dental Clinic Web Design and Visual Proof

sections.text: When building modern medical and dental websites, user trust is everything. Patients want to see real evidence of what a clinic can achieve before they schedule an appointment. During the development of [CarePulse / Aura Dental Studio](/projects/11/), one of the primary client requirements was an interactive 50/50 before-and-after comparison slider that works smoothly on both desktop touchpads and mobile touch screens.

Many developers rely on heavy third-party UI packages for basic image comparisons. However, writing a lightweight, custom React component gives you full control over performance, bundle size, and touch event handling. Let us break down how to implement this cleanly using React 19 and TypeScript.

sections.title: Building the Before-and-After Image Comparison Slider Component

sections.text: The core logic relies on tracking mouse and touch coordinates within the container bounds, converting those pixel values into a percentage, and applying that percentage to clip the top image element using CSS properties.

sections.title: Performance Optimization Note
sections.text: By calculating widths relative to container bounding client rectangles instead of forcing layout recalculations on every frame, this slider runs smoothly at 60 frames per second without lagging mobile devices.

sections.title: Designing a Multi-Step Medical Booking Flow UI

sections.text: A complicated booking form causes patients to abandon their appointments before finishing. The key to a high-performing medical booking flow UI is breaking down information collection into small, digestible steps: selecting the treatment category, picking a date and time slot, and entering contact details.

items: Step 1: Choose procedure type (e.g., Dental Implant, Teeth Whitening, Routine Cleaning)
Step 2: Select preferred doctor and available time slot
Step 3: Collect patient contact info with inline form validation
Step 4: Show instant confirmation screen with calendar sync options
